name: Affine Oriented-Matroid Tope Classes Have Matroidal Shadows
statement: If $C$ is the projection of the $g=+$ topes of an oriented matroid $M$, then $\operatorname{Sh}(C)=\operatorname{Ind}(M/g)$. In particular its shattered complex satisfies matroid augmentation. The common shadow of the remote rooted pair violates augmentation: $\{1,2\}$ and $\{1,5,6\}$ are faces but neither $\{1,2,5\}$ nor $\{1,2,6\}$ is. Every higher paired-square level also violates augmentation. Hence none of these rooted pairs is a full affine-oriented-matroid tope class.
proof: A support is shattered by the full antipodal tope set exactly when it is independent in the underlying matroid. Antipodality identifies shattering of $I$ in the positive half with shattering of $I\cup\{g\}$ in the full tope set, which is equivalent to independence of $I$ in $M/g$. The displayed face pair gives an explicit augmentation failure at level zero; at higher levels the fresh root pair is a maximal two-face while adjoining either fresh coordinate to a shattered old pair gives a three-face, again violating augmentation.
comments: This excludes representation as the full positive half of one oriented matroid. It does not exclude fibers with several sign constraints or representations using auxiliary elements.
